headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Western Russia: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, just now: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: US Army eyes developing soldier-worn drone detection gear.
The Army is in the early stages of developing and testing a wearable or lightweight device that could alert soldiers to the presence of hostile drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Russian forces attacked the city of Bakhmach in Chernihiv Oblast with Banderol drone-launched cruise missiles on the morning of 16 October, causing extensive damage and leaving four people in need of medical treatment.
- The Moscow Times, just now: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region.
The plant in Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Zelenskyy: Europe understands that as long as Ukraine holds out, escalation with Russia will be lower.
Zelenskyy has said Europe is united because it sees the risks, citing Russian drone incursions, and warned Ukraine’s collapse would be a bigger threat to the EU.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Trump slams Ukraine’s decision to resume energy strikes as a ‘disgrace’.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Trump slams Ukraine’s decision to resume energy strikes as a ‘disgrace’.
Ukraine had paused strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after Trump’s ceasefire announcement.
- Balkan Insight, 8 hours ago: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.

The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration.
Draft conclusions backed by Rome, Warsaw and Copenhagen say irregular migration is "negatively linked to crime rates."

[Dabanga] Furawiya / Karnoi / El Tina / Umm Darfa / El Rosei -- Drone attack in Furawiya area of North Darfur kills two and injures eight, while a Red Crescent volunteer dies in a bombing in Blue Nile and South Darfur authorities impose sweeping emergency measures.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: Houthis struck Riyadh airport 20 times in October, Saudi-led coalition says.
Yemen’s Houthi rebels have struck Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport 20 times since the start of October. A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said the attacks involved 10 drones, four ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and two unidentified projectiles.

Angry families and political supporters packed the courtroom as Sibeko faced charges linked to a shooting that killed four people and wounded three others.

[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 7 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Poverty, Injustice Threaten Lasting Peace in Zimbabwe - ZPP.
[263Chat] The Zimbabwe Peace Project (ZPP) has called for greater investment in justice, human rights and inclusive institutions warning that poverty, inequality and weak access to justice continue to threaten lasting peace in Zimbabwe.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: South Africa: Authorities Shut Down March and March Arrest Claims.
[Scrolla] The National Prosecuting Authority says no warrant was issued and that it takes no instructions from political parties or public office holders. KwaZulu-Natal police say they have no trace of any case registered against the two and urge activists not to make reckless statements.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.
- The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Trump banking on ‘swift end’ of Iran war to bring down fuel prices.
• Pezeshkian decries US blockade, insists ‘military force’ will not compel Tehran into submission • Washington weighs using ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ against Iranian energy sites, CNN reports WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump once again predicted a swift end to the war with Iran, and a sharp drop in oil prices once the conflict concludes, even as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force them into submission. “The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana.
- The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
India - bottom line: 'Ensure safety of Indians': MEA's strong message to US after Hindu temple 'attack' plot.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: 'Ensure safety of Indians': MEA's strong message to US after Hindu temple 'attack' plot.
Authorities in Aurora thwarted a disturbing mass-shooting scheme aimed at a local Hindu temple. In light of this, the Indian ministry of external affairs voiced alarm over the rise in hate crimes in the United States. A 19-year-old suspect now faces charges for threatening the temple while armed. Meanwhile, Indian-American organizations are mobilizing to spotlight anti-Indian sentiment and exploring collective response strategies.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Middle East oil returns, does that mean that Iran has lost control of Hormuz?.
The US war with Iran exposed Tehran’s ability to disrupt the global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, around 19 million barrels of crude oil were exported daily from the Middle East. However, September data from tanker-tracking firm Kpler showed oil flows recovering to an average of 16 million barrels per day, the highest since the conflict began.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Georgia renter left paralysed by falling tree gets claims revived by appeals court.
William Frank Jennings, a Lindale, Georgia resident, became paralyzed after a tree fell on his house, despite having warned his landlord about its dangerous state. The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that his claims against Romulus Investments were improperly dismissed, noting significant conflicting evidence regarding hazard notifications. This ruling enables Jennings to pursue his case further to potentially establish liability and seek damages for his injuries.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Staying connected under fire: How GSAT-7C will boost IAF's fighting edge.
The Indian Air Force signed a deal for the GSAT-7C satellite to boost its communications capabilities. This satellite aims to enhance secure communications for network-centric warfare beyond traditional networks. It is designed to facilitate real-time connectivity, allowing various military platforms to communicate effectively. Developing this satellite domestically reduces reliance on foreign providers, enhancing India's military autonomy. However, details regarding its specifications and launch date have not been disclosed.

European leaders on Friday rallied around Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky as Kyiv’s ties with US President Donald Trump have nosedived and worries grow that US leader is increasingly siding with Russia.
